div.head: VI As 3
div.ab: Ðridde: þæt we tellan á X menn togædere (⁊ se ýldesta bewiste þa nígene to ælcum þara gelaste þara þe we ealle gecwǽdon) ⁊ syððan þa hyndena heora tógædere, ⁊ ænne hyndenman, þe þa X men mynige to ure ealre gemǽne þearfe; ⁊ hig XI healdan þære hyndene feoh ⁊ wítan, hwæt hig forðsyllan, þonne man gildan sceole, ⁊ hwæt hig eft niman, gif us feoh arise ǽt urum gemǽnum spræce; ⁊ witon eac, þæt ælc gelast forðcume þara þe we ealle gecweden habbað to ure ealra þearfe be XXX pæn̄ oððe be anum hryðere, þæt eall gelæst sy, þæt we on urum gerædnessum gecweden habbað ⁊ on ure forespæce stænt.

Tertium: ut computemus decem homines simul; et senior (ex eis) nouem conseruet ad omnes impletiones eorum que diximus. Et postea ipsi hyndeni obaudiant simul et uni hyndeno homini, qui ipsos (illos) decem homines commoneat ad omnium nostrum commune commodum. Et ille XI. custodiat ipsorum hyndenorum pecuniam et sciat, quid ipsi mittent, quando ipsi gildare debebunt, et quid recipiant, si nobis pecunia surgat a (de) nostra communi locutione. Et sciant etiam, ut omnis executio proueniat eorum quę simul ediximus ad nostram omnium utilitatem per XXX den. uel unum animal (hoc ualens), ut hoc totum impleatur, quod in nostra consultatione dictum est uel in nostra prelocutione stat.

Ðridde: Þæt we tellan á X menn togædere, ⁊ se ýldesta bewiste þa nígene to ælcum þara gelaste þara þe we ealle gecwǽdon; ⁊ syððan þa hyndena heora tógædere, ⁊ ænne hydenman, þe þa X men mynige to ure ealre gemǽne þearfe; ⁊ hig XI healdan þære hyndene feoh, ⁊ wítan hwæt hig forð syllan, þonne man gildan sceole, ⁊ hwæt hig eft niman, gif us feoh arise ǽt ure gemǽnan spræce; ⁊ witon eac, þæt ælc gelast forðcume þara þe we ealle gecweden habbað to ure ealra þearfe be XXX pǽn oððe be anum hryðere, þæt eall gelæst sy, þæt we on urum gerædnessum gecweden habbað ⁊ on ure forespæce stænt.

Drittens: dass wir je zehn Mann zusammenzählen — und der [an Rang] älteste die neun [übrigen] zu jeder der Leistungen anleite, die wir alle bestimmt haben — und sodann die Hundertverbände von ihnen zusammen’ und [je] einen Hundertoberen [bestimmen], welcher jene zehn [ältesten] Männer zu unser aller gemeinsamem Nutzen anhalte; und diese elf sollen das Geld des Hundertverbands bewahren und vermerken, was sie ausgeben, wenn gezahlt werden muss, und was sie hinwiederum einnehmen, wenn uns von unserem gemeinsamen Klaganspruche Geld erwächst; und sie sollen auch beobachten, dass jede der Abgabenleistungen eingehe, die wir alle [oben] bestimmt haben zu unser aller Nutzen, [nämlich] bei 30 Pfennig [Vermögen] oder bei einem Rinde, dass alles erfüllt werde, was wir in unseren Beschlüssen bestimmt haben und [was] in unserer Vereinbarung steht.

Thirdly: that we count men together in groups of ten — and let the senior [in rank] direct the [other] nine in each of the obligations that we have all determined — and then [group] their hundreds together and [appoint for each] one head of the hundred, who is to urge those ten [senior] men on to the common benefit of us all; and these eleven are to keep the money of the hundred and note what they pay out when payment must be made, and what they in turn take in if money accrues to us from our common suit; and they are also to see that every one of the contributions comes in which we have all determined [above] for the benefit of us all, [namely] at 30 pence [of property] or at one head of cattle, so that everything is fulfilled that we have determined in our ordinances and [that] stands in our agreement.

Third: We shall always count ten men together, and the chief man shall see that the [other] nine shall discharge all the dues which we have all agreed upon; and then [we shall count] them in groups of a hundred, with one official for the hundred who will admonish those ten [chief men] for the common benefit of us all. And these eleven shall keep the money of the hundred-group and an account of what they disburse when money has to be paid; and again, of what they receive when money accrues to us through a plea we have made in common. And they shall see to it also that each of those dues is forthcoming on which we have all agreed for our common benefit, on penalty of thirty pence or one ox; that everything may be fulfilled, which we have declared in our ordinances, and which stands in the terms of our constitution.

Thirdly: that we always are to reckon 10 men together- and the senior is to have charge of the nine in all those dues which we have all agreed on- and afterwards a hundred of them together, and one hundred-man, who is to admonish those 10 men to the common benefit of us all; and those 11 are to have control of the money of the hundred, and to note what they pay out, when one has to pay, and what on the other hand they receive, if money comes to us from our common suit; and they are to see to it also that each due is forthcoming which we have all agreed to for the benefit of us all, on penalty of 30 pence or one ox, so that all may be performed which we have agreed in our ordinances and which is set out in the terms of our constitution.
div.note: Liebermann would correct H's ‘ure gemæne’ to ‘ure gemænan’ (Price and followers).

Die 10- und 100-Verbände werden also erst hiermit geschaffen, sind nicht schon ältere Einrichtungen. Der 10-Verband heisst teoðung 8, 1; s. Gl Zehnerschaft 1e. f. 8c. Diese Zehn- und Hundert-Verbände stehen nicht etwa ausserhalb (unter) der Gilde; denn 15 Zeilen weiter bestimmen diese Organe über ‘unser’ Geld. Offenbar neu gezählte Zehnerschaften und Hunderte, und nicht etwa alte Gilden, werden hier zusammengefasst: eine Einteilung, nicht eine Vereinigung liegt vor

The groups of 10 and of 100 are thus only created by this, and are not already older institutions. The group of ten is called teoðung 8, 1; see Gl Zehnerschaft 1e. f. 8c. These groups of ten and of a hundred do not stand, say, outside (below) the guild; for 15 lines further on these bodies make decisions about ‘our’ money. Evidently newly counted tithings and hundreds, and not, say, old guilds, are combined here: what we have is a division, not a union
conservet Q ungenau, eher ‘beaufsichtige, überwache, regiere’
conservet Q inexact, rather ‘supervise, oversee, govern’

Richtig trennt K. Maurer diesen persönlichen 100-Verband vom territorialen Hundred; s. d. Gl 10a; Wb: hynden. [Keineswegs hiess hynden später tithing (gegen Earle Landcha. l) oder war identisch mit hynd (gegen Kemble Cod. dipl. V p. xxx) in Bi 1208 oder bedeutete, wie hund ursprünglich, ‘Dekade’; gegen Price, Leo Rect. 177, Lewis Laws of Wales 284.] Dass diese Abteilung der Gliederung des Geschlechts entspreche (Brunner II 286) seh ich nicht. — Diese Verbände können nicht genau 100 Personen umfassen, da die Gildenzahl nicht gerade durch 100 teilbar, noch auch für die Ausfüllung der Zahl bei Sterbefällen Fürsorge getroffen und das Zusammenhalten Verwandter wohl das Gewöhnliche war. — Mehrere Hundert-Verbände in der Gilde bestehen auch nach 8, 1. So ist auch hier nicht, wozu die ungeschickte Sprache verführen kann, nur Ein Vorsteher zu verstehen

K. Maurer rightly distinguishes this personal group of a hundred from the territorial hundred; see that word in Gl 10a; Wb: hynden. [By no means did hynden later mean tithing (against Earle Landcha. l), nor was it identical with hynd (against Kemble Cod. dipl. V p. xxx) in Bi 1208, nor did it mean ‘decade’, as hund originally did; against Price, Leo Rect. 177, Lewis Laws of Wales 284.] I do not see that this division corresponds to the structure of the kindred (Brunner II 286). — These groups cannot have comprised exactly 100 persons, since the number of guild members was not necessarily divisible by 100, nor was any provision made for making up the number in the event of deaths, and keeping relatives together was probably the usual practice. — Several hundred-groups exist within the guild according to 8, 1 as well. So here too, despite what the clumsy wording may lead one to think, not just a single headman is to be understood
statt heora hatte wohl die Vorlage Q’s hyra, das er hyran verlas und hyndenman regierend dachte. Kemble (Brit. Review 1841, 85) will tyn hinter hyndena ergänzen: sinngemäss, aber unnötig

instead of heora Q’s exemplar probably had hyra, which he misread as hyran and took as governing hyndenman. Kemble (Brit. Review 1841, 85) would supply tyn after hyndena: right in sense, but unnecessary

Toller compares hundredmann: centurio; see Gl Hundred 25. a
Ellipse im Original, ergänzbar aus dem ‘Anordnen’ in tellan Z. 1
Ellipsis in the original, to be supplied from the ‘arranging’ in tellan l. 1
d. h. die Zehnerschaftsvorsteher zur Gildepflicht
i.e. the headmen of the tithings, for the guild duty
Q, hig auslassend, missversteht die Zahl als ‘elfter’, den Hundertvorsteher allein. Die folgenden Plurale sprechen dagegen
Q, omitting hig, misunderstands the number as ‘eleventh’, i.e. the headman of the hundred alone. The plurals that follow tell against this

Die Hundertagentur ist nur Teil der Gildenkasse, einnehmend und ausgebend in deren Auftrag. Gewinn und Verlust trifft die Gilde; denn mindestens 240 Personen, also mehr als Ein Hundertverband, bringen den Ersatz für einen verlorenen Sklaven auf; 6, 3. Auch die Spurfolgepflicht belastet nicht die Hundertbrüder allein, sondern die Gildegenossen; 4

The hundred agency is only part of the guild fund, receiving and paying out on its behalf. Gain and loss fall on the guild; for at least 240 persons, i.e. more than one hundred-group, raise the replacement for a lost slave; 6, 3. The duty of following the trail, too, is a burden not on the members of the hundred alone, but on the guild members; 4
nicht ‘wissen’ nach Q, oder ‘decide’ (Price, Kemble Saxons I 242)
not ‘know’, following Q, nor ‘decide’ (Price, Kemble Saxons I 242)

Die Ausgabe ist die der Gilde, da sie hier man oder ‘wir’ heisst im Ggs. zu ‘ihnen’, jenen Agenturverbänden. Sie deckt Ersatz des Versicherten, Wergeld an Ungenossen für Totschlag durch einen Genossen im Gilden-Interesse, Buss- und Strafgeld im Falle verlorenen Prozesses, Kosten der Kriminalpolizei und des Strafvollzugs, vielleicht auch Geschenke an Richter und König

The expenditure is that of the guild, since the guild is here called man or ‘we’ in contrast to ‘them’, those agency groups. It covers replacement for the insured member, wergild to non-members for a homicide committed by a member in the guild’s interest, compensation and fines in the event of a lost lawsuit, the costs of the criminal police and of carrying out punishments, and perhaps also gifts to judges and king
Über das Genus s. Wb: spræc II; Genus 3; vgl. 6, 1¹
On the gender see Wb: spræc II; Genus 3; cf. 6, 1¹

‘after the rate of’ ‘im Verhältnis von’ verstehen Price, Schmid. Dies bezöge sich auf 30 Pf. in 2. Bessere aber vielleicht Übs.: ‘bei Strafe von 30 P. oder einem R.’. Dies ist die Ungehorsamsbusse der Gilde 6, 2. 7. 8, 5; vgl. Wb: be 8

Price and Schmid understand ‘after the rate of’ (‘im Verhältnis von’). This would refer to the 30 pence in 2. But perhaps better to correct the translation to: ‘on penalty of 30 p. or an ox’. This is the guild’s compensation for disobedience 6, 2. 7. 8, 5; cf. Wb: be 8
Vielleicht nur wortreiche Tautologie, ohne sachlichen Unterschied vom folgenden ‘Vereinbarung’. Der Plural kann singularisch dieses Eine Stück VI As bezeichnen
Perhaps merely a wordy tautology, with no difference in substance from the following ‘agreement’. The plural may denote, as a singular, this single piece VI As
Q übersetzt silbenhaft; ‘agreement’, wie Thorpe, Wbb. und Edd. übersetzen, scheint sonst unbelegt; doch heisst formæl, forword ‘Vertrag’
Q translates syllable by syllable; ‘agreement’, as Thorpe, the dictionaries and the edd. translate, seems not to be attested elsewhere; but formæl, forword mean ‘contract’
This group of a hundred associates (hynden) is, of course, quite distinct from the territorial hundred.

Thorpe and Schmid understand ‘be xxx p.’ to mean ‘after the rate of 30 pence’ (cf. cap. 2); but I have followed Liebermann’s suggestion (iii. p. 119) that a better translation would be ‘bei Strafe von 30 P. oder einem R.’ (cf. cap. 6 § 2, below), 30 pence being the fine for insubordination enacted by the guild (cf. cap. 8 § 5, below).
